If you're not in a rush to grab Apple products on launch day and are willing to wait, the Apple Certified Refurbished store has always been a solid choice. Generally speaking, about three months after a new product launch, certified refurbished versions start appearing on Apple's official website.

Other companies offer similar options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but it's worth noting that the quality standards and warranty terms vary across programs……

Apple Certified Refurbished Products

When shopping at the Apple Certified Refurbished store, you typically get around 15% off, and the products themselves are almost indistinguishable from brand-new ones. Specifically, Apple promises all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing by Apple
  • Like-new appearance with no marks or scratches
  • Brand-new battery with the same battery life as a new product
  • All original accessories and cables included
  • Same one-year Apple standard warranty as new products
  • AppleCare+ can be purchased additionally

Basically, the only difference you'll notice is that the product comes in a plain white box instead of the original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed may offer more competitive pricing, but keep in mind you won't get the same quality assurance:

  • Inspection and testing are handled by the seller, not Apple
  • The appearance is pre-owned—expect marks and scratches (see image below)
  • The battery is used and only guaranteed to retain at least 80% of original capacity
  • Accessories may not be genuine Apple products
  • 90-day Amazon warranty provided, instead of Apple's one-year warranty

Regarding marks and scratches, Amazon offers three quality grades:

  • Premium / Excellent: No visible imperfections when viewed from 12 inches away
  • Good: Only minor scratches, barely noticeable when held at 12 inches from a handheld device
  • Acceptable: Visible and tactile scratches

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored's descriptions are far more vague than Amazon's, with very ambiguous wording—it's unclear what you'll actually receive:

  • No promises about cosmetic condition, only claiming to deliver "like-new performance and reliability"
  • Beyond the above description, no specific information about battery condition is provided
  • No information provided about accessories
  • Warranty provided by the seller, not Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier comes with a one-year seller warranty, while Like New, Good, and Fair tiers only get 90 days. The company's specific definitions for each tier are unclear.

9to5Mac's Take

If you want something that looks identical to a brand-new product and comes with Apple's warranty, the Apple Refurbished store is clearly the top choice.

That said, Amazon Renewed pricing can indeed be significantly lower, and if you're willing to accept the trade-offs mentioned above, it's still a decent option. Especially if you're planning to take our advice and get the iPhone 17 Pro instead of this year's latest model to save some money (you won't get a cable either way), here are some attractive deals:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,214 (original price $1,499) — all-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,215 (original price $1,499) — all-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,208 (original price $1,499) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,164 (original price $1,299) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,170 (original price $1,299) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,171 (original price $1,299) — only $1 above all-time low price

As for Walmart Restored, I have reservations because their guarantees are too vague, but if you're not satisfied, you can indeed opt for a return.
